AgentEnrollRequest.description: Binds an unguessable householdHash bucket to a householdId label + token verifier. Carries no key material.

publicKey.description: base64 of exactly 32 bytes (Ed25519 public key); the private half never leaves the device

EncryptedEnvelope.description: E2E v2 wrapper around a SyncEnvelope. Server stores bytes only; see docs/e2e-v1.md. v1 SyncEnvelope is unchanged.

entity.description: standalone ingredient/step envelopes are rejected (fold into the parent recipe pre-encrypt)

householdHash.description: hex(SHA256("smidgen-hh-v1" || syncCode || householdId)); must equal the :hash path param

kid.description: opaque per-household key id; feeds the HKDF info string

id.description: stable client-generated id, echoed back and preserved across updates
stable client-generated id, echoed back and preserved across updates

PhotoKeys.description: R2 keys. URL signing <15min. Variants thumb/1024/original.

id.description: stable client-generated id, echoed back and preserved across updates

AgentToken.description: Key-derived bearer (base64url of 32 HKDF-SHA256 bytes, domain-separated from the data key — see docs/agents/). Enroll via POST /agent/enroll, which stores only hex(SHA256(token)). Accepted as an alternative to the Ed25519 device signature on every mutating route (prod): reads are scoped to the enrolled household (out-of-scope reads are 404), writes require an explicit matching householdId (else 403). Blind /v2 envelopes stay opaque — the server verifies the token, never content.
AgentToken.name: x-agent-token

DeviceSig.description:
base64 Ed25519 signature over the canonical string METHOD + "
" + path+query + "
" + ts + "
" + hex(SHA256(bodyBytes)) (empty body hashes as hex(SHA256(""))). Required on every POST/PUT/DELETE except POST /v2/devices; GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, /health and /openapi.json stay open. Unknown / stale / revoked keys get 401 (self-revoke = logout).
DeviceSig.name: x-device-sig

DeviceTs.description: millis since epoch, digits only; |now - ts| <= 5 min. Replay window is a documented limitation (no server nonce ledger).
DeviceTs.name: x-device-ts

info.description: Single Hono Worker + D1 + R2. MIT only. See packages/contracts/README.md.
info.title: Keep Cooking API

post.description: Bind a householdHash bucket to a plaintext householdId label plus a token verifier (hex(SHA256(raw agent token))). Open: knowledge of the unguessable householdHash IS the capability. Re-enroll to rotate the token without rotating the data key. Never receives key material.

409.description: householdId label already bound to a different hash (present the existing agent token in x-agent-token to re-bind it)

post.description: Stateless JSON-RPC 2.0 (Streamable HTTP subset): initialize (legacy handshake, kept for 2025 clients), server/discover (modern handshake), tools/list, tools/call, ping. Every tool call authenticates via x-agent-token; tools are scoped to the enrolled household. Tool schemas are versioned in packages/contracts/mcp-tools.json.

202.description: notification accepted (no body, per Streamable HTTP)

get.description: Serve R2 photo bytes for a signed URL minted by GET /photos/sign (or the photos_sign MCP tool, which targets this route). Verifies the HMAC exp/sig first; no device signature or agent token required (the signature IS the capability, expiring in <15min).

404.description: photo serving unconfigured or key does not exist

post.description: Open enrollment — no device signature required (this is how devices join). 201 on first enroll, 200 on idempotent re-enroll with the same key, 410 when the id was revoked (gone, enroll a fresh deviceId instead), 409 when the id is already enrolled with a different key, 400 on validation failure. Reads stay open; every other write requires the enrolled key (see DeviceSig).

200.description: already enrolled with the same key (idempotent)

409.description: device id already enrolled with a different key

410.description: device id was revoked (gone) — enroll a fresh deviceId instead

post.description: Signed revocation (caller signs with its own enrolled key). Revoking your own key is logout — the next write from that key gets 401 (device revoked). There is no shared token to rotate; enroll a fresh deviceId instead (re-enrolling this revoked id returns 410).

401.description: missing / unknown / stale / bad / revoked device signature

200.description: stored ids (stale writes are idempotent no-ops)

413.description: batch exceeds E2E_MAX_PUSH_BATCH (500 envelopes) — chunk and retry. Native outboxes must split large backlog drains into <=500-envelope pushes.
